newsitem.title: UK: London LDCs soften despite Russia roadshow news.
newsitem.headline: London LDCs soften despite Russia roadshow news.

text.p: News that Russia will begin roadshowing its debut Eurobond on November 11 failed to lift emerging debt prices in London, which limped towards the weekend on New York's softness.

Traders were cheered by news that Russia was going ahead with the Eurobond, an expected $500 million five-year issue, despite news yesterday that the IMF had left Moscow without deciding to pay the latest tranche of a $10 billion three-year loan -- due chiefly to worries over tax revenues.
"It's good news -- they're saying forget the IMF, we're going ahead with the Eurobond anyway," said one fixed income analyst here.
"Fundamentally we can't believe that Russia would issue a Eurobond that would be anything other than a great success," he said. "There is massive pent-up demand for east Europe."
Traders are now looking for a Eurobond launch around the last week of November -- after the November 13 FOMC meeting.
The analyst said the Eurobond would have a beneficial effect mainly on MinFins 3 and 4, lending them support.
"In terms of strategy, if you want to keep playing with Russia stick to MinFins 3 and 4, which are supported by arbitrage against the Eurobond," he said.

The MinFin 3 RU3E99=RR, which matures in 1999, eased about 1/8 to 81-1/4 on screen. One trader said MinFins inched up fractionally late on Thursday when the news first trickled into the market of the roadshow dates.
Dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR held steady at 75-1/4.
Elsewhere in eastern Europe, Bulgarian debt continued to worry investors.

An IMF mission is due to arrive in Sofia next week and analysts say it is anyone's guess whether the Fund will decide to release the delayed second tranche of a standby loan which will haul the country back from the brink of default.
"I'd love to recommend people buy Bulgaria, but it would be irresponsible," said one emerging debt analyst here.
Prices will rise as soon as the release of the $115 million tranche is announced, but he said buying call options was a safer bet than Bulgarian debt proper due to their more limited downside.
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were quoted at 43-7/8, 1/4 down on their 43-5/8 close yesterday.
Latin American paper saw little London action after continuing their slide in New York.
Foreign & Colonial Emerging Markets said in a note to investors that the Latin American fixed income rally was over after providing year-to-date returns of around 30 percent.

The sentiment change was due to a variety of factors, including Mexican peso weakness, concerns over the Russian IMF developments and the desire of players to reap profits in time for their year-end bonuses, it said.
Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were quoted up 1/16 at 68-3/4 while Mexican Pars MX625L19=RR were flat at 58-3/4 and Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR held steady at 79-3/4.

One dealer said traders were keeping an eye on U.S. durable goods and existing homes sales data due later today, but were beginning to look towards next Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls for October. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
